title: NPR review describes Trump administration actions against perceived targets
description_medium: An NPR review published April 29, 2025, counted more than 100 people and organizations the Trump administration had targeted during his first 100 days, from prominent politicians to international students. It described criminal investigations, ICE detention, security-clearance revocations, firings and contract restrictions. NPR also reported that courts often blocked challenged actions, while Trump allies defended the administration as restoring the rule of law.
description_long:
NPR’s April 29, 2025 review surveyed federal actions during the first 100 days of Trump’s second term and identified more than 100 perceived targets, including political opponents, former officials, news organizations, universities, law firms and international student protesters. It described use of criminal investigations, ICE detention, firings, revoked security clearances and restrictions on federal contracts. Examples from one April week included probes ordered into two former Trump administration officials, an executive order aimed at a law firm, announced investigations of New Jersey’s governor and attorney general over immigration policies, and sweeping demands sent to Harvard.

The article connected this pattern to Trump’s campaign pledge, “I am your retribution,” and said many statements it reviewed suggested motives involving personal grievances, partisan politics and payback. It also presented competing accounts: Trump allies called the actions a restoration of law enforcement, while people affected described fear, lost income and detention. NPR reported that courts frequently sided with targets who challenged actions, including blocking an order against Susman Godfrey law firm on constitutional or legal grounds. The article’s count and interpretation describe NPR’s review; each individual action had its own target and legal dispute.

corrected_wording.original: Retribution Campaign Fulfillment - 'I Am Your Retribution' Realized
corrected_wording.replacement: NPR review describes Trump administration actions against perceived targets
corrected_wording.reason: The original title asserts that a campaign pledge was fully realized. The linked reporting describes a review of actions and perceived targets, alongside disputes about motive and legality.

source_access_notes: The NPR URL did not load in the reader; read the same April 29, 2025 NPR report as syndicated by North Country Public Radio, including its account of the review, examples, allied response and court challenges.
rationale: NPR’s review substantiates the count of more than 100 perceived targets, describes the listed executive actions and gives both administration allies’ defense and legal challenges. The reporting characterizes the pattern as a retribution campaign, but does not establish that every action was unlawful retaliation.
